T h is appeal coming on for orders this day, t h e cou  following:
 ORDER

This appeal has been filed under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the award dated19.12.2022 passed by 22nd Member MACT Indore in Claim Case No.2697/2017.
2.
The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

As per the findings of the Tribunal,
in case of death of Mohanlal, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.5,54,256/- along with interest from the date of filing of the claim petition till realization.

3. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding just and proper amount of compensation in the case as the amount awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
It is further contended that the Tribunal has committed error in holding that at the time of accident the deceased was earning Rs.6,950/- per month.
It is further submitted that the Tribunal should have considered the statement of Awantibai (AW-1) who clearly stated that at the time of accident the deceased was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
The claimants filed income tax return Ex.P-14 to Ex.P- 19.
So Tribunal committed error in calculating the compensation in lower side.
Hence, Prays for enhancement of compensation.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company supported the impugned award and submitted that Tribunal has awarded just and proper compensation and prays for dismissal of the appeal.
5. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

6. After hearing the learned counsel for the both the parties and on perusal of the record it is found that claimants filed income tax return of the deceased Ex.P-14, Ex.P-16, Ex.P-18 which were filed by the deceased before 3 years of his death.
Claimants were to file only income tax return of the deceased of the year in which deceased died in the accident.
Claimants were unable to give substantial evidence that at the time of accident, the deceased was running grocery shop.
The claimants were unable to file registration of the grocery shop.
The claimants were unable to adduce any evidence that at the time of accident, claimant was skilled person and earning Rs.30,000/-.

2 7.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, in the considered opinion of this Court, the Tribunal has rightly granted just and proper compensation to the claimants.
Hence, there is no need of enhancement of the compensation.
No interference in the impugned award is made out.
Accordingly, the miscellaneous appeal is dismissed.
(HIRDESH) JUDGE RJ Awantbai vs Rajkumar Patidar on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119266071/
